identity.real_world_identity_notes: Brazilian Chevrolet Opala, built by General Motors do Brasil from 1968 to 1992 and a mainstay of Brazilian racing from the 1973 endurance era onward. Its floor-shift manuals were offered in four-speed and five-speed form.

wheel_rim.notes: Observed from the cockpit during the guided drive.

notes: Simulator behaviour was directly observed in a guided drive in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled. There is no automatic cut or blip, so the driver lifts to upshift and blips to downshift.

The gearbox is synchronised, so a downshift blip is authentic technique and eases the synchros but is not needed to engage the gear. It is recorded as optional rather than required, which is reserved for gearboxes that cannot engage without it.

The source lists four-speed and five-speed floor-shift manuals without dating either, so which one a given racing specification used is not established by it; the gear count here comes from the drive.
This class reports a single configuration; the selection screen offers no aero package and only the plain identity has been observed.
The drive found five gears, where the two Stock Cars records in this batch found four. The three are separate selectable identities in separate classes and none inherits from another.
Observed live in AMS2 1.6.9.91 via guided verification observation ams2.chevrolet-opala-old-stock-race.20260816t043241459z-21e51081 by Jason Kinslow.

confidence.basis: Simulator behaviour was live-tested in AMS2 1.6.9.91 with automatic clutch and shifting disabled, and the real-world transmission is supported by registered sources.

claims.basis: A registered source establishes the Opala and its manual gearbox options, and the exact simulator identity was observed live.

The source lists four-speed and five-speed floor-shift manuals, and the live drive selected 5 H-pattern gears with no automatic cut or blip. An ordinary production road-car manual of this period is synchronised.
Directly observed during the guided drive: move-off, shift clutch use, automatic cut and blip, and the cockpit rim.
